Class PlayerDeathDropHandler

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.attachment.PlayerDeathDropHandler
public final class PlayerDeathDropHandler extends Object
Drops (or keeps / destroys) all death-droppable player-scoped attachment contents when a player dies — the player-death twin of BlockScopedDropHandler. Called from com.trevorschoeny.menukit.mixin.PlayerDeathDropMixin at the TAIL of Player.dropEquipment, co-located with vanilla's own keepInventory-gated destroyVanishingCursedItems() + inventory.dropAll().

Closes the death-lifecycle gap: a playerAttached content attachment is registered copyOnDeath (so a KEPT bag carries across respawn), but Fabric's copy is not gamerule-aware — the library owns the keepInventory check and the per-stack drop here. Each stack resolves a DropRule: KEEP stays (copyOnDeath carries it), DROP spawns a vanilla player drop, DESTROY vanishes.

Clear-after-drop is load-bearing. Dropped/destroyed slots are written back EMPTY before respawn's copyOnDeath runs — this prevents a dupe (copyOnDeath would otherwise carry the same items that were just dropped) and, in Phase 2, lets a grave mod's capture-and-clear naturally suppress this drop fallback. Ordering is clean: drop-and-clear runs now (at death), copyOnDeath copies later (at respawn) → a DROP death copies an empty bag, a KEEP death copies the full bag.
